headline: Downside alignment persists as mixed 8:30 ET data precede industrial production and the cash open
body: Before the 8:30 ET releases, Nasdaq-100 futures were 1.17% lower with broad technology and semiconductor weakness, elevated long yields and a two-week-high VIX. The releases were mixed: housing starts missed, permits beat, and import/export prices fell. Fresh post-release NQ bar evidence is insufficient, limiting Tail to a modestly elevated reading ahead of industrial production and the cash open.

lookbackSummary: Published ChatGPT assessments moved from Monday WATCH into low Tail through most of the U.S. session, then rose overnight from WATCH to orange as downside futures, long yields, volatility, technology weakness and geopolitical pressure became more aligned.
outlookSummary: Risk is concentrated through today’s 15:15–16:30 Berlin industrial-production, cash-open and pending-home-sales sequence. Conditional Tail is highest through opening price discovery and then decays if meaningful retracements and cross-asset stabilization appear; FOMC minutes remain the next major policy checkpoint on August 19.

forecast.analysis: Late-morning U.S. structure becomes the main checkpoint. Tail remains at WATCH only if downside efficiency persists; stabilization in semiconductors, megacaps, volatility or yields would support normalization.
Midday conditions are modeled as less event-driven. Persistent cross-asset pressure can keep WATCH active, while balanced breadth and meaningful pullbacks would lower directional-path risk.

Into the U.S. afternoon, Tail is modeled back in the low band unless a second downside leg develops. Oil and geopolitical stress remain background amplifiers but do not by themselves imply one-way NQ structure.
Approaching the cash close, the base case is lower Tail if no renewed directional extension appears. A late-session break that holds near extremes would be the main invalidation.

After the cash close, risk is mainly headline and gap sensitivity. Any late equity-futures continuation would need fresh confirmation; otherwise the path is modeled as mixed with still-high macro and geopolitical stress.
During the daily futures maintenance interval, no new price-path evidence is assumed. Tail is modeled low while unresolved oil, rates and geopolitical drivers keep stress elevated.
At the evening futures reopen, a fresh gap or one-way continuation would raise Tail; an orderly reopen with retracements would keep the assessment in the low band.
Overnight Asia begins with no directional move assumed. Cross-asset alignment, especially yields, oil and technology futures, is the key conditional checkpoint.
Asian-session risk is modeled as normal-to-mixed unless a persistent futures trend develops. The unresolved Hormuz backdrop continues to support elevated stress.
Mid-Asia conditions retain low Tail absent repeated extension. A widening gap with aligned yields and volatility would be the main reason for reassessment.
Toward the Asia-Europe handoff, the forecast remains low Tail unless overnight direction becomes efficient and pullbacks fail.
Early European trading can amplify or challenge the overnight direction. Tail rises only modestly in the forecast unless Europe confirms a persistent NQ move with cross-asset alignment.
European morning risk remains mixed. Oil and long yields stay relevant, while improving breadth or retracements would limit Tail.
Late European morning is modeled with low Tail unless U.S. futures develop a clear one-way structure. No future continuation is assumed.

Approaching U.S. premarket liquidity, Tail edges higher because cross-asset signals can become more informative. Persistent technology weakness plus firmer yields/volatility would be the key conditional amplifier.
U.S. premarket depth increases. Tail remains low unless a directional gap is accompanied by shallow retracements and broad technology/semiconductor confirmation.
With the next U.S. session approaching, conditional WATCH risk begins to rise. The main question is whether overnight pressure persists into deeper liquidity rather than mean-reverting.
Late premarket conditions carry WATCH risk if oil, yields, volatility and technology remain aligned. Conflicting signals or deeper pullbacks would cap Tail.
By the final forecast hour, attention begins shifting toward the later FOMC-minutes session. Event proximity raises stress, but Tail stays WATCH unless an actual persistent price path develops.

forecastDetail.comment: Mixed 12:30 UTC data have not resolved the premarket downside setup; industrial production and the cash open are the immediate checkpoints, with Tail elevated but limited by missing fresh post-release bar evidence.
After industrial production and the cash open, Tail remains elevated only if price discovery extends one-way; pending home sales at 14:00 UTC is an additional checkpoint.
Early cash-session risk stays elevated conditionally on failed rebounds and broad downside confirmation; two-sided trade would reduce Tail.
WATCH is modeled if the opening impulse stops extending; retracement depth and cross-asset stabilization are the key tests.
Residual WATCH risk reflects persistent yields/oil and technology weakness; broader recovery or repeated reversals would favor further decay.
Late-morning risk remains WATCH only if downside efficiency persists; improving semis, megacaps, volatility or yields would weaken the Tail case.
